cards.text: Ezekiel, a prophet, gets a new word from the LORD in the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month. The LORD has spoken about Pharaoh king of Egypt before (Ezekiel 31:2), and now there's more. This time God tells Ezekiel to take up a lament for Pharaoh and say it right to him.
The lament starts with Pharaoh's picture: he's like a lion among the nations, and like a monster in the seas. Friend, MY first introduction was a sticker that said 25 cents.

cards.question: In the lament, Pharaoh is like a monster in the seas. Where does this monster thrash about?
In the lament, Pharaoh thrashes about in his rivers. True or false: he keeps his rivers calm and his streams clear.

cards.text: He churns up the water with his feet and muddies the streams. Then the Lord GOD speaks, and friend, this monster is about to meet his match.

cards.question: Pharaoh is like a monster splashing around in the water. What does the Lord GOD say He'll spread over him?

cards.text: God says a company of many peoples will draw Pharaoh up in His net. From monster of the seas to stuck in a net, and friend, I KNOW that slide, because one day I was king of the counter and the next I was in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Once Pharaoh is hauled out of the water in God's net, where does God say He'll leave him?
Out in the open field, God says no creature will come near Pharaoh.

cards.text: God says the birds of the air will settle on him, and the beasts of the earth will eat their fill.

cards.question: After the birds and the beasts, God says Pharaoh's remains will end up in just one small spot.

cards.text: His flesh goes on the mountains and his remains fill the valleys. His blood will drench the land all the way to the mountains, and the ravines will be filled.

cards.question: When God extinguishes Pharaoh, He turns to the sky over him. What does God say happens to the sun, the moon and the stars?

cards.text: God says every shining light in the heavens will go dark over Pharaoh, and He'll bring darkness on his land. My night sky out back is still waiting on most of its stars, and I'd PANIC if one went out.

God says He'll trouble the hearts of many peoples when He brings Pharaoh's destruction among the nations, in countries Pharaoh doesn't know. When I went into the junk drawer, the news didn't even make it past the dish rack.

cards.question: God says He'll brandish His sword before many peoples. How will their kings react to Pharaoh's fall?

cards.text: On the day Pharaoh falls, each king will tremble every moment for his life. It's like when the big boss gets walked out of the building, and suddenly the whole office shows up EARLY.

cards.question: Then God names whose sword is coming for Pharaoh: 'The sword of the king of ___ will come against you!'

cards.text: That's Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon (Ezekiel 30:10), and God says the swords coming belong to the mighty, the most ruthless of all nations. Not top ten, not honorable mention, friend: NUMBER ONE.

cards.question: The most ruthless of all nations will ravage the pride of Egypt. What does God say happens to all her multitudes?

cards.text: God says He'll slaughter all of Egypt's cattle beside the abundant waters. Remember how Pharaoh was like a monster muddying the streams with his feet?

cards.question: After Egypt's cattle are slaughtered, God says human feet and cattle hooves will keep stirring up Egypt's waters.
With nothing stirring them up, God says He'll let Egypt's waters ___ and make her rivers flow like oil.

cards.text: The thrashing is over. God says He'll make Egypt a desolation, empty it of all that filled it, and strike down all who live there.

cards.question: When God makes Egypt a desolation, what does He say they will know about Him?

cards.text: And it all comes back around to the lament Ezekiel started with. God says this lament will be chanted over Egypt and all her multitudes, and friend, the only song ever chanted over me was the drawer squeaking shut.

cards.question: God says the daughters of the nations will chant this lament over Egypt.
